sections.h2: Which Lyon County offices send, value and collect the bill?
sections.html:
The Lyon County Sheriff collects, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values, and the County Clerk takes over when a bill goes stale after April 15. The Sheriff's own page cites KRS 134.140 and 160.500 as the basis for collecting state, county, school and district tax on real, tangible and intangible property, and says the office handles about seven million dollars a year.

Find the Sheriff at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, Eddyville. Mail goes to PO Box 126, Eddyville, KY 42038. The PVA operates from 500 B West Dale Avenue and answers at 270-388-7271. For prior-year delinquent bills, the Sheriff directs taxpayers to the County Clerk at 270-388-2331.

Both the Sheriff and the PVA work on West Dale Avenue, so one visit can answer two questions. Call before you go: the Sheriff cannot accept money until bills arrive from the clerk around the end of September.

sections.h2: Why is Lyon County unlike most Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Water covers a sixth of the county. Lyon County totals 257 square miles, 43 of them water, with Lake Barkley on the Cumberland River along its south side. Eddyville, the seat, had 2,375 residents in 2020 and neighboring Kuttawa had 629. Both towns were relocated to higher ground when Barkley Dam backed up the lake. The new Eddyville plat was filed on August 13, 1959, and owners of land in the two doomed towns were offered a free lot in the new one.

Interstates 24 and 69 cross at Eddyville, with U.S. 62 and 641 running through the center. Mineral Mound State Park sits on a Lake Barkley peninsula, the Kentucky State Penitentiary stands on the shore south of town, and Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area faces Kuttawa across the water. A single district, Lyon County Schools, serves everyone and enrolled 884 students in 2024 to 2025.

Storms have left marks on the housing stock. An EF4 tornado tore through Eddyville and the county on December 10 and 11, 2021, damaging or destroying hundreds of homes and businesses, and an EF3 touched down near Eddyville on May 26, 2024. If your house was repaired or rebuilt, tell the PVA, because the January 1 value follows the property's condition.

sections.h2: What do the Lyon County numbers suggest about selling?
sections.html:
The market is small and mostly owner-held. Four in five occupied homes are lived in by their owners, and over a quarter of residents are in the retirement-age group. The 2020 census found 4,780 housing units, with 30.4 percent of them vacant.

New building adds little to the roll: the Census Bureau logged just five building permits for 2025. Typical household income in Lyon County runs higher than in Logan County, and so does the typical home value. A seller here often prices against lake access as well as square footage.

sections.h2: What is the Lyon County payment calendar?
sections.html:
Your payment counts if it is received or postmarked by the date shown. The Sheriff gets bills from the clerk late in September, so statements usually reach mailboxes in the first week of October.

  • October 1 through November 1: pay 2 percent less.
  • November 2 through December 31: pay the stated amount.
  • January: add a 5 percent penalty.
  • February 1 through April 15: add a 21 percent penalty.
  • Past April 15: the clerk holds the bill, and further penalties may apply.

No bill by October 10? The Sheriff will send a duplicate. The tax year is the calendar year, so the bill covers January through December of the year printed on it.

The office accepts checks, money orders and cards, with the card processor charging a fee, and the same options are online. Partial payments are refused, though a single payment can cover several bills. For owners who find the lump sum hard, the Sheriff suggests checking for exemptions and asking a lender about escrow.

sections.h2: Who is on the hook for the bill when a Lyon County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the property on January 1 gets the bill, even if the house has since changed hands. The Sheriff says a closing agent or attorney usually works out each side's share of the year. Some agents then pay the Sheriff directly, and in other deals one party receives a credit and pays later.

  • Prorated payments are refused. Someone must pay the full bill.
  • Mortgage companies do not automatically get the statement. Lenders can pull data from the PVA roll, yet the owner must make sure the lender actually has the bill.
  • If a bill arrives in your name after a sale, send it on to the new owner at your former address.

Ask the closing agent to confirm in writing who pays the Sheriff and by when, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: How can a Lyon County owner contest an assessment?
sections.html:
Confer with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk. State rules give you until the end of the workday after the roll's public viewing period closes, and that period opens in early May and runs about two weeks.

A local panel then hears the matter some 25 to 35 days after viewing ends. It wants facts: photographs, an appraisal, insurance policies, construction costs or listings. A written decision explains any change and describes the next step to the state tax appeals board.

Call the PVA at 270-388-7271 each spring for the exact dates, since the window can be shifted and the change is advertised locally.

sections.h2: Which exemptions shrink a Lyon County bill?
sections.html:
Start with the homestead and disability exemptions. A homeowner who lives in the home and is a senior, or is classed as totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. For a house at the county's typical $189,500 value, the taxable base then falls to $140,400.

The Sheriff sends people who struggle to pay toward these exemptions and refers questions about them to the PVA at 270-388-7271. File with the PVA, not the Sheriff or clerk. Disability claimants normally reapply annually, except service-connected veterans and people whom Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled.

sections.h2: What is the best way to sell a Lyon County house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Get the payoff in writing from the correct office and let the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds. This year's balance comes from the Sheriff, and earlier years come from the County Clerk.

Delinquent bills get advertised before any sale, and the county attorney sends notices, so early action avoids added fees. Interest of 1 percent a month starts when the clerk takes the bill, with clerk and attorney commissions on top. Ask the closing agent to pay any recorded lien from the sale proceeds so the house passes to the buyer with a clean tax record.

faqs.q: Where does Lyon County send its property tax payments?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Lyon County Sheriff at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, Eddyville, or by mail to PO Box 126, Eddyville, KY 42038. An online link on the Sheriff's tax page also works. Past April 15, pay the County Clerk.

faqs.q: How large is the Lyon County early-payment discount?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent, for money received or postmarked between October 1 and November 1. The stated amount applies through December 31, and a 5 percent penalty begins in January.

faqs.q: Will the Lyon County Sheriff take a partial payment?
faqs.a: No. Partial payments are refused. A single payment may cover several bills, and the Sheriff suggests checking exemptions or lender escrow if the full amount is hard to meet.

faqs.q: If I sell my Lyon County home in June, who pays that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed, and the closing agent usually prorates each side's share at the table. The Sheriff needs the whole bill paid, so confirm in writing who sends the payment.

faqs.q: How much is the Lyon County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, for seniors and totally disabled owners living in their homes. Apply through the PVA at 270-388-7271.
